segment_reference_payload.description: Segment loads data into Snowflake via S3 staging with COPY INTO. All staging files are CSV format with gzip compression. Column names follow Segment conventions (snake_case, lowercase in source but Snowflake stores as uppercase by default).

staging.copy_command: COPY INTO <schema>.<table>(<columns>) FROM '<s3_path>' CREDENTIALS=(...) PATTERN='.*\.csv\.gz' FILE_FORMAT=(TYPE=csv FIELD_OPTIONALLY_ENCLOSED_BY='"' ESCAPE_UNENCLOSED_FIELD=NONE) TRUNCATECOLUMNS=TRUE

tracks.description: One row per track event. Table name: TRACKS (uppercase).

identifies.description: One row per identify event. Table name: IDENTIFIES (uppercase).

users.description: Deduplicated user traits table. Merged from identifies via primary key ID. Table name: USERS (uppercase).

pages.description: One row per page event. Table name: PAGES (uppercase).

screens.description: One row per screen event. Table name: SCREENS (uppercase).

groups.description: One row per group event. Table name: GROUPS (uppercase).

aliases.description: One row per alias event. Table name: ALIASES (uppercase).

column_naming.convention: Segment uses snake_case column names. Snowflake stores identifiers as uppercase by default when unquoted. Segment columns appear as uppercase in Snowflake (e.g., ANONYMOUS_ID, USER_ID, RECEIVED_AT).
column_naming.context_flattening: Nested context fields are flattened with underscore separators: context.library.name → CONTEXT_LIBRARY_NAME
column_naming.properties_flattening: Event properties are flattened as top-level columns: properties.product_id → PRODUCT_ID
column_naming.traits_flattening: Identify traits become top-level columns in IDENTIFIES and USERS: traits.email → EMAIL

loading_method.merge_strategy: Append-only for event tables (TRACKS, IDENTIFIES, PAGES, SCREENS, GROUPS, ALIASES). USERS table is deduplicated/merged.
loading_method.deduplication: Uses uuid_ts column for deduplication in USERS table merge

rudderstack_expected_payload.description: RudderStack loads data into Snowflake via S3/GCS/Azure Blob staging with COPY INTO, or via Snowpipe Streaming API (RudderStack-unique). Staging files are CSV format with gzip compression. Column names are UPPERCASE (Snowflake provider case convention applied via ToProviderCase).

staging.copy_command: COPY INTO <schema>."<table>"(<columns>) FROM '<storage_path>' <auth> PATTERN='.*\.csv\.gz' FILE_FORMAT=(TYPE=csv FIELD_OPTIONALLY_ENCLOSED_BY='"' ESCAPE_UNENCLOSED_FIELD=NONE) TRUNCATECOLUMNS=TRUE

snowpipe_streaming.description: Snowpipe Streaming is a RudderStack-unique loading method that uses the Snowflake Snowpipe Streaming API for low-latency ingestion. Not available in Segment.
snowpipe_streaming.latency: Near real-time (seconds vs minutes for batch COPY INTO)

tracks.description: One row per track event. Table name: TRACKS (uppercase, via ToProviderCase for SNOWFLAKE).

columns.CONTEXT_LIBRARY_NAME: VARCHAR — SDK library name (rudder-sdk-js, rudder-sdk-go, etc.)

identifies.description: One row per identify event. Table name: IDENTIFIES (uppercase). Primary key: ID.

users.description: Deduplicated user traits table. Merged from identifies via MERGE statement with staging table. Primary key: ID (derived from USER_ID). Table name: USERS (uppercase).

merge_strategy.description: RudderStack uses staging table + MERGE INTO for USERS table deduplication. allowMerge config controls this behavior. When merge is disabled or table is in appendOnlyTables, append-only mode is used.
merge_strategy.merge_window: Configurable per-destination via Warehouse.snowflake.mergeWindow.<dest_id>.column and .duration. Default column: RECEIVED_AT.

pages.description: One row per page event. Table name: PAGES (uppercase).

screens.description: One row per screen event. Table name: SCREENS (uppercase).

groups.description: One row per group event. Table name: GROUPS (uppercase).

aliases.description: One row per alias event. Table name: ALIASES (uppercase).

rudder_discards.description: RudderStack-specific table for tracking discarded columns that exceed schema limits. No Segment equivalent.

rudder_identity_merge_rules.description: RudderStack-specific identity merge rules table used for warehouse identity resolution.

rudder_identity_mappings.description: RudderStack-specific identity mappings table for resolved identity graph in warehouse.

column_naming.convention: RudderStack applies ToProviderCase(SNOWFLAKE, name) which uppercases all identifiers. All column names are stored as UPPERCASE in Snowflake.
column_naming.context_flattening: Nested context fields are flattened with underscore separators: context.library.name → CONTEXT_LIBRARY_NAME
column_naming.properties_flattening: Event properties are flattened as top-level UPPERCASE columns: properties.product_id → PRODUCT_ID
column_naming.traits_flattening: Identify traits become top-level UPPERCASE columns: traits.email → EMAIL

loading_method.merge_strategy: Configurable via allowMerge (default: true). Staging table created, data COPY'd in, then MERGE INTO target table for USERS. Event tables (TRACKS, IDENTIFIES, etc.) default to append-only unless merge is configured.
loading_method.deduplication: Uses UUID_TS column and configurable merge window (column + duration) for dedup in MERGE operations. Primary key maps: USERS→ID, IDENTIFIES→ID, RUDDER_DISCARDS→ROW_ID.
loading_method.append_only_tables: Configurable via Warehouse.snowflake.appendOnlyTables — tables listed here skip merge and use append-only loading

iceberg_support.description: RudderStack supports Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables as an alternative table format. When EnableIcebergSetting is true, CREATE OR REPLACE ICEBERG TABLE syntax is used with CATALOG='SNOWFLAKE' and an external volume.

data_type_mapping.description: RudderStack maps internal types to Snowflake types via standardTableManager.dataTypesMap

staging_file_format.rudderstack: CSV with gzip compression (primary). Snowpipe Streaming uses internal Snowflake ingestion format.
staging_file_format.parity_gap: Both use CSV for batch loading. RudderStack additionally supports Snowpipe Streaming API which bypasses file staging entirely.

object_storage.rudderstack: S3, GCS, or Azure Blob staging depending on cloudProvider config. Also supports Snowflake internal staging via storage integration.
object_storage.parity_gap: RudderStack supports broader staging options (GCS, Azure). Segment is S3-only for Snowflake staging.

column_naming_conventions.segment_columns: Lowercase snake_case in event spec (anonymous_id, user_id, received_at). Stored as UPPERCASE in Snowflake due to default unquoted identifier behavior.
column_naming_conventions.rudderstack_columns: Explicitly uppercased via ToProviderCase(SNOWFLAKE, name). All columns stored as UPPERCASE (ANONYMOUS_ID, USER_ID, RECEIVED_AT).
column_naming_conventions.parity_status: Functionally equivalent — both result in UPPERCASE columns in Snowflake. No naming convention gap for standard columns.

context_library_name.parity_gap: Different SDK library identifiers — expected difference, not a parity issue

rudderstack_additional_columns.LOADED_AT: RudderStack adds a LOADED_AT timestamp column to track when data was loaded into the warehouse. Not present in Segment.
rudderstack_additional_columns.RUDDER_DISCARDS_TABLE: RudderStack creates a RUDDER_DISCARDS table for tracking columns that exceeded schema limits. No Segment equivalent.

identity_tables.segment: Segment does not create identity tables in the warehouse. Identity resolution is handled externally by Segment Unify.
identity_tables.rudderstack: RudderStack creates RUDDER_IDENTITY_MERGE_RULES and RUDDER_IDENTITY_MAPPINGS tables for batch warehouse-level identity resolution.
identity_tables.parity_gap: RudderStack performs identity resolution at the warehouse level; Segment handles it in the Unify service. Different architectural approach.

snowpipe_streaming.segment: Not available. Segment uses batch COPY INTO exclusively for Snowflake loading.
snowpipe_streaming.rudderstack: Snowpipe Streaming API available as alternative loading method. Provides near real-time data availability (seconds vs minutes).
snowpipe_streaming.parity_gap: RudderStack-unique feature. Provides lower latency data availability in Snowflake.

internal_vs_external_staging.segment: External staging only (S3 → COPY INTO with AWS credentials).
internal_vs_external_staging.rudderstack: Both internal staging (via Snowflake storage integration) and external staging (S3/GCS/Azure Blob with credentials). Auth method determined by destination config: AWS credentials or STORAGE_INTEGRATION setting.
internal_vs_external_staging.parity_gap: RudderStack supports storage integration (internal staging) in addition to external credential-based staging.

merge_behavior.segment: Append-only for event tables. USERS table is deduplicated.
merge_behavior.rudderstack: Configurable merge via allowMerge config (default: true). Supports append-only mode per table via appendOnlyTables config. USERS table uses staging table + MERGE INTO with configurable merge window (column + duration) and duplicate sampling for debugging.
merge_behavior.parity_gap: RudderStack provides more granular merge control (per-table append-only, configurable merge windows, duplicate detection/sampling).

table_format.rudderstack: Standard Snowflake tables (default) or Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables (when EnableIcebergSetting is true). Iceberg tables use different column type mappings (e.g., number(10,0) for int, timestamp_ntz(6) for datetime, varchar for json instead of variant).
table_format.parity_gap: RudderStack-unique feature. Iceberg table support provides open table format compatibility.

delete_support.rudderstack: Configurable DeleteBy operation via enableDeleteByJobs config. Supports deletion by user_id across specified tables.
delete_support.parity_gap: Both support deletion. RudderStack implementation is configurable per destination.

notes: Snowflake shared warehouse destination. Key parity gaps: staging file format, column naming conventions. Snowpipe Streaming API is RudderStack-unique. Reference: gap report warehouse payload comparison table. RudderStack integration source: warehouse/integrations/snowflake/. Both platforms use S3-based CSV staging with COPY INTO as the primary loading method. Column naming is functionally equivalent (both uppercase in Snowflake). Major RudderStack differentiators: Snowpipe Streaming for near real-time loading, Iceberg table format support, multi-cloud staging (S3/GCS/Azure), configurable merge windows, warehouse-level identity resolution tables (RUDDER_IDENTITY_MERGE_RULES, RUDDER_IDENTITY_MAPPINGS), and fine-grained append-only table configuration.
